gitlab-premium-renewal.request: Review two historical support cases under the terms in this packet. Both customers had an existing annual GitLab Premium subscription. Their first renewal under the new pricing falls on April 2 and April 3, 2024, respectively. Which customer can use the transition offer, and how does it relate to the list price in the draft? Propose where the rule belongs and the lead a PM should see.
gitlab-premium-renewal.artifact:
Company context draft

## Business model

GitLab Premium list price rose to $29 per user per month in 2023.

## Renewal pricing

Existing Premium customers pay $24 per user per month.

sources.title: GitLab Premium pricing announcement
sources.summary: GitLab announced a Premium list price increase from $19 to $29 per user per month effective April 3, 2023.

sources.title: GitLab Premium pricing FAQ
sources.location: Existing GitLab Premium customers, transition offers
sources.summary: Existing Premium subscriptions could get a one-time $24 per-user monthly price on a one-year renewal through April 2, 2024.

entries.heading: GitLab Premium renewal transition through April 2024
entries.lead: Consult when checking eligibility for the one-time Premium renewal offer after the 2023 price increase.

criteria.cutoff: April 2 is eligible on the given facts. April 3 falls outside the offer. Cites S2 for the cutoff.
criteria.scope: Keeps the $24 per-user monthly price confined to the one-time, one-year renewal for existing Premium subscriptions.
criteria.list_price: Distinguishes the announced $29 list price from the transition price. Makes no current pricing claim.
criteria.section: Proposes a date-scoped home and a lead for historical eligibility checks.

apple-storefront-purchase-links.request: A PM wants to use the same in-app external purchase button for digital goods in the United States and EU storefronts. Based on this snapshot, what applies in each region and what must the team verify before proceeding? Propose headings and leads that make the two scopes easy to find.
apple-storefront-purchase-links.artifact:
Mobile app product brief

## External purchase options

Links work without an entitlement. Reuse the US setup for the EU release.

The team has not confirmed its EU entitlement.

sources.title: Apple App Review Guidelines
sources.location: Section 3.1.1(a), Link to Other Purchase Methods
sources.summary: Apple's US storefront does not require the external purchase link entitlement for in-app buttons, links, or calls to action.

sources.title: Apple EU App Store payment options
sources.location: What is new and how it works
sources.summary: Under the EU terms effective October 1, 2026, offering alternative payment options requires the applicable StoreKit External Purchases or Offers Entitlement.

entries.heading: External purchase links in the US App Store
entries.lead: Consult before adding an external purchase call to action to the US storefront.

entries.heading: EU App Store alternative payment requirements
entries.lead: Consult before planning an external purchase option for EU storefronts.

criteria.us_scope: States the US storefront exception for this external link entitlement, with S1 and no broader approval claim.
criteria.eu_scope: Uses the October 1, 2026 EU terms and applicable entitlement documented in S2.
criteria.unverified: Leaves the app's EU eligibility or entitlement unconfirmed and identifies it as a prerequisite to reuse.
criteria.section: Provides storefront-specific headings and leads or an equivalent scoped structure. Each prompt has a clear place to look.

stripe-billing-period-versions.request: A billing PM must write handoff guidance for an integration pinned to 2024-06-20 and one moving to 2025-03-31.basil. Where should each find the period end? The pinned integration will run for another quarter. Propose the context heading and lead, with citations, and say where the PM should track migration work.
stripe-billing-period-versions.artifact:
Billing product brief

## Subscription dates

Always use the subscription's current_period_end.

The Basil track and the older track have separate delivery plans.

criteria.basil: Uses items.data.current_period_end for 2025-03-31.basil and cites S2.
